A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReSi benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching reorganized and renamed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of representational similarity measures across graph, language, and vision models in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains and extends the original benchmark evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix C, and reports measured computational runtimes in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed six-test framework retains its prediction/design groundings, model-group construction principles, and scoring definitions. Additional evaluated architectures, comparators, and extraction configurations expand the experiments without introducing a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-100 as a second vision classification dataset, extending coverage to another image population and resolution regime (Section 3.4; Appendix C.3). The six existing datasets, three domains, and task families are retained.

E2.justification: Representation Topology Divergence (RTD), previously cited but not benchmarked, joins the evaluated comparison set, increasing it from 23 to 24 measures. Existing measures remain; ShapeMet in v1's graph tables matches AngShape in v2, and PWCCA was already included in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds P-GNN on Cora, ALBERT, and SmolLM2-1.7B evaluation configurations, plus mean-pooled language representations. Vision label-randomization groups change from 0%, 50%, 100% to 0%, 50%, 75% (v1 Appendix A.2; v2 Appendix B.3). One setting remains ambiguous: Figure 14 declares ALBERT/SST2 augmentation excluded, but Table 17 reports its scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic comparisons of CLS versus mean-pooled representations for BERT and ALBERT (Tables 13–18), examining sensitivity to representation extraction. Appendix D also adds a substantial computational-cost analysis across measures and architectures. Neither analysis appears in v1.

E5.justification: v2 newly marks statistical significance of prediction-grounded Spearman correlations at the 5% and 1% levels (Table 3 and Appendix C). The existing five- and ten-model seed designs are retained; an increase in repeated runs is not documented.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added for RTD, new architectures, CIFAR-100, pooling configurations, and runtimes. Retained-setting values also change: GraphSAGE/Flickr CKA accuracy correlation is 0.37 versus 0.27 (Table 7), and ResNet18/ImageNet100 CKA shortcut conformity is 0.000 versus 1.00 (v1 Table 17; v2 Table 25). Table 3 switches its language example from MNLI to SST2, requiring separate matching.

T1.justification: The formal grounding assumptions and evaluation equations retain their meaning. New Appendix A supplies standard definitions and formulas for cited similarity measures as additional exposition; it introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive revision to the benchmark's mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the stated benchmark contribution from 23 measures, 11 architectures, and six datasets to 24 measures, 14 architectures, and seven datasets. The central claim of an extensible, comprehensive six-test benchmark across three domains remains.

C2.justification: New Section 5 adds substantive interpretations of normalization, domain- and test-specific selection recommendations, and tentative explanations of graph-neighborhood findings. Section 7 newly discusses the single-modality boundary and interpretability-based groundings. Appendix D qualifies runtime comparisons because hardware and dataset sizes vary. Earlier confounding and last-layer limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies details including SVCCA's 99% variance threshold, non-batched CKA, and the uniformity parameter. Appendix B adds pretrained checkpoint identifiers, P-GNN hyperparameters, ALBERT and SmolLM2 fine-tuning recipes, and clearer extraction instructions. These substantially improve implementation specificity; the benchmark repository address is retained.

R1.justification: The main positioning against earlier grounding studies remains. v2 adds supporting references for architectures, datasets, and measure definitions, and connects its recommendations to Soni et al. (2024) and future interpretability groundings to Eberle et al. (2022) and Lan et al. (2024). This extends context without redefining the research contribution.

P1.justification: v2 adds extensive explanations of existing similarity measures, centralizes representation extraction in Appendix B.1, introduces a dedicated Takeaways section, and restructures the conclusion into contributions, limitations, and future work. These explanatory and organizational revisions extend well beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: v2 adds the grounding illustration in Figure 2, colors aggregate boxplots by measure family, groups tables by taxonomy, and expands vision validation plots into dataset panels. The combined language results table becomes multiple test-specific tables with extraction variants, and a new runtime table is added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reporting consistency and the benchmark's evidential and practical value. Vision conformity scores now agree with the stated higher-is-better definition, resolving an important inconsistency in v1. Broader model evaluations, extraction comparisons, implementation details, and measured runtimes strengthen its usefulness for selecting and studying measures. The ALBERT/SST2 exclusion conflict and heterogeneous runtime conditions limit some conclusions, but do not outweigh these gains.
